description: Hi! I am Krishna Mahajan, a 1st-year B.Tech Computer Science student specializing in Cybersecurity. I build robust solutions using C, C++, Java, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, backed by strong UI/UX design knowledge. As a solo participant for CodeZero working on Earth System trends, I bring end-to-end technical execution—from secure, data-driven coding to clean, intuitive interfaces. Let's build something impactful!
summary:
**GeoTrend Detective – Turning Earth Observation Data into Environmental Insights**

GeoTrend Detective is an interactive web-based tool developed to help students, researchers and environmental enthusiasts investigate changes in Earth's systems over time. Users can explore environmental variables, select geographical locations, compare two regions, analyse historical trends and visualize patterns through statistical graphs.

The platform includes ready-to-explore demonstration case studies, live NASA POWER data retrieval for custom locations, and CSV analysis for datasets obtained from resources such as NASA Giovanni and AppEEARS. It applies statistical techniques including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Theil-Sen slope estimation and the Mann-Kendall test to identify trends and assess their significance.

By making Earth observation data easier to explore and interpret, GeoTrend Detective helps users distinguish meaningful environmental changes from random fluctuations. It encourages data-driven investigation, improves scientific understanding and makes satellite-based environmental analysis more accessible to a wider audience.
details:
Project Details – GeoTrend Detective-CodeZero

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

GeoTrend Detective is an interactive, browser-based environmental data analysis platform designed to help users investigate changes in Earth's systems over time. It works like a digital scientific case file, allowing users to explore environmental variables, investigate geographical locations and determine whether observed changes represent meaningful trends or random fluctuations.

Users can begin with a guided investigation wizard or choose a ready-made case study. They can select environmental variables, define a time period, choose geographical regions and compare two locations to understand how environmental conditions differ.

The platform also allows users to investigate custom locations anywhere on Earth by searching for a place, entering latitude and longitude, selecting a map point or drawing a geographical box. It retrieves real monthly data for supported variables through the NASA POWER API. Users can also upload or paste CSV datasets exported from NASA Giovanni, AppEEARS or other sources.

The platform processes the data by removing seasonal patterns, calculating trends and applying statistical methods, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Theil-Sen slope estimation and the Mann-Kendall test. It presents the results through time-series graphs, confidence intervals, statistical indicators and plain-language explanations.

2. What benefits does it provide?

  • Makes environmental and satellite-based data easier to explore and understand.
  • Helps users identify long-term environmental changes rather than relying on isolated observations.
  • Enables comparison of environmental trends across different geographical regions.
  • Provides statistical evidence to help determine whether observed trends are significant.
  • Supports both real NASA POWER data and externally uploaded environmental datasets.
  • Makes scientific analysis more accessible to students, researchers and the general public.
  • Encourages data-driven environmental investigation and scientific learning.

3. What is the intended impact?

The intended impact of GeoTrend Detective is to make Earth observation data more understandable, accessible and useful for environmental investigation.

Environmental changes such as temperature variation, precipitation patterns, soil moisture and solar radiation can have important consequences for ecosystems, agriculture, water resources and communities. However, interpreting long-term datasets and understanding statistical trends can be difficult for people without a scientific or technical background.

GeoTrend Detective aims to reduce this barrier by transforming environmental datasets into understandable visual evidence and explanations. It encourages users to ask scientific questions, investigate geographical differences and make evidence-based observations about changes happening across our planet.

Ultimately, the project aims to connect satellite data with real-world environmental understanding and promote wider participation in Earth science.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware and software were used?

Programming languages and technologies:

  • HTML5 – Structure and content of the web application.
  • CSS3 – Styling, responsive layouts and the vintage scientific case-file appearance.
  • JavaScript – Interactive features, data processing, statistical calculations, charts and API communication.
  • SVG – Data visualizations and graphical elements.

Data sources and services:

  • NASA POWER API – Retrieval of real environmental data for custom geographical locations.
  • NASA Giovanni – External source of downloadable Earth observation datasets.
  • NASA AppEEARS – External source of geospatial and satellite datasets.
  • NOAA and other scientific resources – Additional environmental data and research references.

Development and deployment software:

  • GitHub – Source-code hosting and version control.
  • GitHub Pages – Hosting and publishing the web application.
  • Modern web browser – Running and testing the application.
  • Google Fonts – Typography used in the interface.

Hardware: A standard computer or laptop was used for development and testing. The application runs in a web browser and does not require specialised scientific hardware.

The project is implemented as a single static HTML file, with its CSS and JavaScript included in the application.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creative aspect of GeoTrend Detective is its combination of environmental science, statistical analysis and an investigative experience.

Instead of presenting users with complicated scientific dashboards, the project uses a detective-themed interface that turns environmental analysis into an interactive investigation. Users explore environmental variables as cases, examine geographical locations as evidence and receive scientific findings as investigation reports.

Its key creative elements include:

  • A guided detective wizard that helps users choose what to investigate.
  • An interactive geographical selection system for custom locations.
  • A two-region comparison system for discovering contrasting environmental trends.
  • A combination of parametric and non-parametric statistical techniques.
  • An automatic explanation panel that translates statistical findings into simpler language.
  • A vintage classified-document visual identity that makes scientific exploration engaging and memorable.

This approach combines scientific functionality with an educational and user-friendly experience.

6. What factors did the team consider during development?

The development focused on several important factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using established statistical techniques to identify and evaluate environmental trends.
  • Data reliability: Distinguishing synthetic demonstration datasets from real NASA observations.
  • Accessibility: Making the application understandable to users without advanced scientific knowledge.
  • Geographical flexibility: Allowing investigations across different locations and regions.
  • Transparency: Displaying statistical methods, confidence intervals, data sources and limitations.
  • Usability: Keeping the investigation process simple and interactive.
  • Performance: Building a lightweight browser-based application that does not require specialised installation.
  • Educational value: Encouraging users to understand not only what is changing, but also how to interpret the evidence.
